system: You are an expert reviewer of machine-learning research ideas.
user:
Compare two research ideas for the SAME research problem and pick the stronger one.

Research problem: Can MVFA's few-shot inference be made inductive, scoring each image only with statistics of the K normal support images and source-validation data instead of test-set min-max normalisation, while keeping image AUROC within 1 point of the re-run transductive baseline and making each image's score invariant to the composition of the rest of the test set (prevalence 10-50%, with and without outliers)? The replacement is evaluated component by component (normalisation, then fusion weight, then image-level aggregation), with sensitivity at 95% specificity and expected calibration error reported alongside AUROC.

A stronger idea is one whose proposed change acts on the SPECIFIC mechanism of the target method that causes the problem (here: the released MVFA code and its verified behaviour), rather than a generic improvement that would apply to any anomaly detector.

Judge on:
1. Specificity. Would this idea plausibly solve THIS problem in THIS method better than a generic alternative? A mechanism that applies equally to any model and any problem is WEAKER, not stronger, because it does not explain why it fixes this problem.
2. Evidence. Is the proposed mechanism supported by the cited literature or by verified properties of the code and the benchmark?
3. Testability. Does the idea make a concrete, falsifiable prediction that can be checked on BMAD with one Colab GPU?

Explicitly DO NOT reward: length or polish of the write-up, stacking many modules, vague "add an attention/adapter module" proposals, or ideas that need data, labels or compute that are not available.

Idea A:
TITLE: Random-effects meta-analysis across MVFA levels and branches for per-image scores
SUMMARY: Treat each of MVFA's level-branch maps as a separate study estimating how abnormal an image is, with its own support-derived standard error, and pool them with a DerSimonian-Laird random-effects model so that inconsistent levels are down-weighted for that image.
HYPOTHESIS: Random-effects pooling across the eight level-branch estimates improves image AUROC by at least 0.5 points over equal-weight averaging of standardised scores on held-out modalities, and the per-image heterogeneity statistic I^2 is higher on false positives than on true positives at the support threshold.
RATIONALE: The Cauchy parent combines dependent p-values validly but treats every level as equally informative for every image. By analogy with meta-analysis, where several studies estimate one effect with different precision and some disagree beyond chance, each level-branch pair gives an estimate (a standardised score) with a precision that can be estimated from the support set; a random-effects model weights precise, consistent levels more and quantifies their disagreement for the specific image. Disagreement among levels (high I^2) is itself a warning sign that is not available from any single fused score.
METHOD: 1) For level l and branch b: effect y_lb = (s_lb - mu_lb)/sigma_lb with support LOO statistics; within-study variance v_lb = 1 + 1/K (uncertainty of the support estimates). 2) DerSimonian-Laird: Q, tau^2 = max(0, (Q - 7)/(sum w - sum w^2 / sum w)), pooled y* = sum w*_lb y_lb / sum w*_lb with w* = 1/(v + tau^2). 3) Image score = y* / SE(y*); report I^2. 4) The correlation between levels is ignored in the weights (documented limitation; Cauchy combination as comparison). 5) test_few.py: implement; remove min-max. No training.
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2,4,8,16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws. Baselines: transductive MVFA pipeline, support z-score. Conditions: equal-weight average of standardised scores; fixed-effect pooling; random-effects pooling; Cauchy combination. Metrics: image AUROC, I^2 distribution for true and false positives, score shift under resampling. Falsified if random effects do not beat equal weighting by 0.5 AUROC points.

Idea B:
TITLE: Empirical-Bayes shrinkage of support statistics for stable per-image MVFA scores at small K
SUMMARY: Stabilise the support-derived normalisation statistics used for per-image scoring by shrinking each branch's support mean and spread toward priors learned across source modalities, with the amount of shrinkage set by K, as in small-area estimation.
HYPOTHESIS: Empirical-Bayes shrinkage of support statistics reduces the across-draw standard deviation of image AUROC at K = 2 and K = 4 by at least 40% relative to raw support statistics, keeps mean image AUROC within 1 point of the transductive pipeline, and has no effect (within 0.3 points) at K = 16.
RATIONALE: The conformal parent treats the support set as the whole reference, which is unstable at K = 2. By analogy with small-area estimation in survey statistics, where estimates for small groups are shrunk toward a population prior in proportion to their uncertainty, the support statistics of an unseen modality can borrow strength from the distribution of such statistics across source modalities. The prior captures how support means and spreads typically relate across modalities; with large K the target's own data dominate, so nothing is lost when data are plentiful.
METHOD: 1) On source episodes (all source modalities, 200 episodes, K matched), record per branch and level the support LOO mean mu and log-std lsd; fit a normal prior over (mu, lsd) per branch and level (mean m0, variance v0) after centring each modality on its own large-sample statistics. 2) On the target: shrunk mu' = (v0 mu_hat + (s^2/K) m0') / (v0 + s^2/K), with m0' the prior mean expressed relative to the target's level-wise text-anchor similarity (a covariate available without labels); same for lsd. 3) Standardise test scores with (mu', exp(lsd')); fuse by averaging; image score top-1% mean. 4) test_few.py: implement; remove min-max. No adapter training.
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2,4,8,16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws. Baselines: transductive MVFA pipeline, support z-score. Conditions: raw support statistics; shrinkage; oracle statistics from 200 target normals (upper reference). Metrics: mean and across-draw std of image AUROC per K, realised specificity at the support threshold, score shift under resampling. Falsified if shrinkage does not reduce across-draw std by 40% at K <= 4.

Respond in exactly this format:
REASONING: <one to three sentences explaining your choice>
CONFIDENCE: <HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW>
WINNER=<A | B | TIE>
